article.summary: Incumbent Surinderpal Rathor was at home Saturday, Oct 17 where he anxiously awaited election results. Preliminary results from this year's municipal election in Williams Lake. Official results won't be declared until Wednesday, Oct. 21. Also at home Saturday, Oct. 17 was former mayor and
article._excerpt: Incumbent Surinderpal Rathor was at home Saturday, Oct 17 where he anxiously awaited election results. Preliminary results from this year's municipal election in Williams Lake. Official results won't be declared until Wednesday, Oct. 21. Also at home Saturday, Oct. 17 was former mayor and challenger Walter Cobb where he too awaited election results. Incumbent Surinderpal Rathor will remain mayor of Williams Lake for a second term following this year’s municipal election. According to preliminary results that were shared approximately 50 minutes after voting closed 8 p.m. at Marie Sharpe Elementary School, Rathor was identified as the successful candidate against challenger and former mayor Walt Cobb. Rathor was elected mayor in 2022 after serving as a city councillor for more than 20 years. Rathor was at home with family, friends and supporters eagerly awaiting for the results to come in, shortly after which he shared a Facebook post. “Thank you for trusting me to continue serving as your mayor. To my wife, family, campaign team and this incredible community thank you for believing in me,” he wrote. “I’m honoured, grateful and ready to keep working for you. Together we can!” In 2014 and 2018 Rathor was defeated by Cobb for the top position. Preliminary results which won’t be made official until Wednesday, Oct. 21, show Rathor securing 2,116 votes (913 advance and 1,203 general) compared to Cobb’s total of 1,026 (530 advance and 496 general). Councillor incumbents Scott Nelson and Michael Moses were also successfully re-elected. New faces set to take up a councillor seat include Ruth Lloyd and Nathan Wiebe with past city councillors Jason Ryll and Paul French returning. City of Williams Lake chief election officer Ross Coupé said there were a total of 3,182 ballots cast. Preliminary results show incumbent Sheila Boehm unsuccessful in her re-election efforts. Coun. Joan Flaspohler, Jazmyn Lyons and Angie Delainey did not seek re-election.

Of the 7,806 estimated eligible voters in the Quesnel civic election, only 2,539 rose to the occasion and chose to keep a few familiar faces on council. Oakes won the mayoral race with 2,137 votes, defeating incumbent Ron Paull, who received 324 votes, according to results posted by Civic Info BC. The third mayoral candidate, Brian Waters, received 58 votes. Four incumbent city councillors were re-elected, with Mitch Vik receiving 1,066 votes, Scott Elliot earning 1,009, Tony Goulet securing 940 and Laurey-Anne Roodenburg receiving 890. Incumbents Debra McKelvie and Martin Runge did not receive enough votes to be re-elected, with 750 and 725 votes respectively. Newcomers Jeremy Drew and Ryan Adams also earned seats on council, receiving 1,281 and 809 votes, respectively. Drew received the highest vote total among the councillors listed. In an interview with the *Observer,* Oakes said the result came as a surprise and that she is grateful for the support from the community. “I want to recognize that I’m excited for an incredible team of councillors that have been elected. I think there is some great diversity, and I think we have a lot of work to do,” she said. “I very much look forward to getting to work with all of them soon.” According to Oakes, she connected with Ron Paull and thanked him for his many years of service. “I very much appreciate and I am grateful for all of the work that he has done,” she said. “I also wanted to recognize the important role that he’ll play in the upcoming 100th anniversary and so many exciting events that are going to be in the community.” Oakes also recognized all the other candidates that put their name forward for city council, regional district and school district. “We had absolutely top-notch people. As glaciers retreat, similar disasters could become a growing danger in mountainous coastal regions.

However, this damage was reversed over time after people quit the drugs.
